original_abstract.text: Fine-grained mixture-of-experts (MoE) models commonly increase expert count by narrowing each expert, treating expert shape as a by-product of routing granularity. LatentMoE moves expert computation into a lower-dimensional space, exposing the input dimension and intermediate width of each expert as explicit design choices. We show that an expert's local Jacobian rank is jointly bounded by these two dimensions, and that balancing them maximizes the rank ceiling at fixed per-expert parameters. Controlled shape sweeps across model scales and routing granularities consistently favor near-square experts. We further use layerwise intrinsic dimension (ID) to guide capacity allocation across depth, co-varying the number and shape of experts while keeping per-layer parameter count, activated FLOPs, and communication volume constant. Compared with layer-homogeneous baselines, our ID-guided allocation achieves lower validation loss and stronger downstream performance. These results establish expert shape and layerwise allocation as practical design axes for MoEs.
original_abstract.source_title: Shaping Latent Mixture-of-Experts: From Expert Geometry to Layerwise Capacity Allocation

en.text: The study treats latent-MoE expert input dimension and intermediate width as separate design variables, linking their balance to a local Jacobian-rank ceiling. Controlled sweeps favor near-square experts. Layerwise intrinsic-dimension-guided allocation improves validation loss and downstream results while keeping each layer's parameters, active FLOPs and communication volume fixed. Expert shape is a transferable design hypothesis, not a verified recommendation gain.

zh.text: 专家数量增加时，专家本身应做成什么形状也会影响能力。该研究分析潜空间MoE的输入维度与中间宽度，实验更支持接近方形的专家；再按各层的内在维度分配专家数量和形状。在逐层参数、激活FLOPs及通信量不变时，验证损失和下游表现改善。推荐MoE能否复现这种收益仍待检验。

original_abstract.text: LLM-augmented data workflows often involve multiple heterogeneous models operating over substantial shared context, such as schemas, tool specifications, interaction history, and intermediate results. Although prefix caching can reduce prefilling overhead, existing approaches are largely limited to reuse within the same model because KV states are tightly coupled to model-specific architectures. We present MapFlow, a system for efficient heterogeneous LLM serving via cross-model attention map reuse. Instead of reusing KV states, MapFlow reuses attention maps, which capture token dependency patterns and are more transferable across models. To enable efficient and accurate reuse, we combine partial recomputation with lightweight linear translation across layers and heads. To make attention reuse practical for long contexts, we further introduce block-level sparse compression and a fused retrieval kernel. Experiments show that MapFlow reduces prefilling latency and improves end-to-end serving efficiency while preserving generation quality across heterogeneous model pairs and multi-turn routing workloads. These results suggest that attention maps provide an effective reusable state for heterogeneous LLM serving, especially in prefix-heavy data workflows. Our code is available: https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/MapFlow.
original_abstract.source_title: Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse

en.text: MapFlow reuses attention maps across heterogeneous LLMs processing shared context, combining partial recomputation, lightweight layer/head translation, block-sparse compression and a fused retrieval kernel. Experiments report lower prefill latency and better end-to-end serving efficiency while preserving generation quality across tested model pairs and multi-turn routing workloads. Cross-model attention reuse could inform shared-context serving, with recommendation gains unverified.

zh.text: 不同模型处理同一段历史时，通常无法直接共享各自的KV状态。MapFlow转而复用注意力图，再用部分重算和轻量映射适配不同层与注意力头，并配合块稀疏压缩和融合内核。在所测模型组合及多轮路由任务中，预填充更快、端到端服务效率更高且生成质量保持；推荐服务收益仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: Large language models are increasingly deployed in applications that act on users' long-term behavior histories, from personal assistants to recommendation and advertising systems. These applications demand the user dimension of LLM intelligence: inferring a person's preferences, intent, and likely future actions from weeks to years of behavior data. Yet current models are trained on static text or synthetic data, neither of which captures how user behavior evolves over time. Real-world behavior records, already available at scale on content platforms and in personal-assistant agents, offer a natural supervisory signal. We propose user behavior as supervision and introduce Vela, a framework that converts real user behavior data into trainable tasks and trajectories. From the anonymized behavior records of 100,000 users, Vela generates 100,000 tasks across 91 real-world task templates; difficulty-based filtering and trajectory acceptance criteria retain approximately 75,000 tasks with selected training trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on these trajectories improves performance over the base model by up to 11.5 points on user-related tasks and by an average of 4 points on general benchmarks. Training on more user behavior data further improves user-related performance, and reinforcement learning after fine-tuning outperforms reinforcement learning from the base model by up to 7.7 points. These gains suggest that real-world user behavior is a scalable source of supervision for both user-centered capabilities and the broader intelligence of LLMs.
original_abstract.source_title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence

en.text: Vela converts anonymized user-behavior records into supervised tasks and training trajectories, combining task templates, difficulty filtering and trajectory acceptance criteria. Fine-tuning a Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model improves the evaluated user-related tasks and general benchmarks, and the authors report further gains when increasing behavior-training data and adding reinforcement learning. For recommendation research, the relevant contribution is a reusable way to turn long-term behavior into user-modeling supervision. Its evidence concerns language-model task evaluations, not industrial CTR lift or a fitted recommendation scaling law, so broader transfer remains to be tested.

zh.text: Vela将匿名用户行为记录转成监督任务与训练轨迹，结合任务模板、难度筛选和轨迹接受条件构造训练数据。微调Qwen3.6-35B-A3B后，所测用户相关任务和通用基准有所改善；作者还报告增加行为训练数据及后续强化学习的收益。推荐研究可借鉴的是把长期行为转成用户建模监督的流程。证据来自语言模型任务评估，不能视为工业CTR提升或已拟合的推荐扩展定律，更广泛的迁移仍需验证。

original_abstract.text: Hybrid language models interleave Gated DeltaNet (GDN) layers, whose recurrent memory has a fixed size, with full-attention layers, whose key-value (KV) cache grows with the context and dominates serving memory. In this paper, we ask whether the recurrent memory already knows what the attention memory will need. We first show that which GDN heads of Qwen3.8-27B keep long memories is fixed by the weights rather than by the document. Next, we define the future utility of a KV entry by how much removing it changes the attention output over the model's own continuations, and find that the write gate, decay and write magnitude that GDN layers emit during prefill anticipate this utility before any query is seen. Because the relation is spread across many GDN heads and layers, and a linear map recovers its trend but less of its high-utility tail than a nonlinear one, we propose GateSight, which learns it with lightweight per-head multilayer perceptrons that read these signals and no attention score. Their predicted utility decides which entries each attention layer keeps, and how much each layer keeps is set by the model's native attention output gate, whose mean differs by more than an order of magnitude across layers. Finally, at serving time, GateSight scores the cache once after prefill and physically releases discarded KV entries. Experimental results on SCBench and RULER-4096 with Qwen3.8-27B and, with the same recipe, the sparse-attention model Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, up to the 262K-token limit of the models, show that with a tenth of the attention KV cache, GateSight is the most accurate of five query-agnostic methods on three of the four model-benchmark pairs and leads KVzip on all four, by 9.5 to 47.2 points. Notably, it scores a full-length context with negligible overhead relative to prefill.
original_abstract.source_title: GateSight: Recurrent Memory Anticipates Attention Memory for Query-Agnostic KV Eviction in Hybrid LLMs

en.text: GateSight learns per-head predictors from recurrent-layer write, decay and magnitude signals to estimate the future usefulness of attention-cache entries before a query arrives. It scores once after prefill, sets layer budgets using native attention gates and physically evicts discarded entries. On two Qwen3.8 models with SCBench and RULER-4096, retaining one tenth of the attention KV cache ranks first among five query-agnostic methods on three of four model–benchmark pairs. It suggests reusing recurrent signals for hybrid long-history memory allocation, but requires learned predictors and is not a model-independent guarantee. Transfer to recommendation is untested.

zh.text: GateSight用循环层的写入、衰减和更新幅度信号训练逐头预测器，在查询到来前估计注意力缓存的未来用途。预填充后只评分一次，以模型原生注意力门控分配各层预算，并实际释放淘汰项。在两种Qwen3.8模型的SCBench和RULER-4096测试中，保留十分之一注意力KV缓存时，四组模型—基准组合中三组在五种查询无关方法中排名第一。其可借鉴点是用循环信号分配混合长历史记忆，但需要训练预测器，并非适用于任意模型的保证。向推荐任务迁移仍未验证。

original_abstract.text: Distributed training of sparsely activated mixture-of-experts (MoE) models is often bottlenecked by workload imbalance and all-to-all (A2A) communication induced by dynamic token routing. Existing token deduplication, expert placement, and replication techniques alleviate these bottlenecks but do not jointly capture their distinct load semantics. Under hierarchical token deduplication, communication counts each token once per destination group at each hierarchy level, whereas expert computation processes every token-expert assignment. With replication, both costs depend jointly on physical layout and token-to-copy mapping, making separate optimization suboptimal. We present PlaceMoE to address this coupling. First, we formulate the joint optimization of expert layout and source-aware token-to-copy mapping for E experts distributed across P devices, accounting for both hierarchical communication traffic and expert-compute load. Second, we develop a solver that combines co-selection-aware expert grouping, bounded dynamic programming for replica allocation, and alternating refinement of layout and mapping. Third, PlaceMoE overlaps replica-gradient synchronization with attention backward. We evaluate PlaceMoE on a 32-GPU cluster and a 64-NPU cluster using Qwen3-VL and DeepSeek-V3. Experimental results show that PlaceMoE achieves up to a 6.94x speedup in A2A communication and 1.74-2.33x speedups in end-to-end training over the state-of-the-art training framework VeOmni.
original_abstract.source_title: Accelerating MoE Training through Expert Placement and Replica Coordination

en.text: PlaceMoE jointly plans expert replicas, physical placement, and source-aware token-to-copy dispatch, distinguishing deduplicated communication from token–expert compute load. It also overlaps replica-gradient synchronization with attention backpropagation. GPU/NPU-cluster tests show faster steady-state training than the evaluated systems on Qwen3-VL and a six-MoE-layer DeepSeek-V3 configuration. Initial profiling, calibration, and planning are excluded from headline step timings, and extra replicas consume memory. CTR engineering inference: co-optimize placement and dispatch for distributed expert rankers using topology-calibrated costs, then include planning amortization and replica memory in end-to-end comparisons. These are language/multimodal-model systems experiments, not CTR experiments.

zh.text: PlaceMoE 联合规划专家副本、物理放置和按 token 来源选择副本的派发映射，分别建模去重后的通信量与 token–专家分配产生的计算量，并将副本梯度同步与注意力反向计算重叠。在 GPU/NPU 集群上，Qwen3-VL 及仅保留六个 MoE 层的 DeepSeek-V3 配置，其稳态训练速度优于所比较系统。主要单步计时不包含初始采样、校准和规划，额外副本也占用显存。对 CTR 的工程启发是依据拓扑校准的成本联合优化分布式专家排序器的放置与派发，并计入规划摊销和副本内存。本文没有 CTR 实验。

original_abstract.text: Foundation models need to support diverse inference budgets, yet training a separate model for each budget duplicates pretraining effort. Elastic models train several nested sub-networks inside one weight-shared supernet, but existing recipes face three obstacles: variable per-step workloads that hinder distributed scaling, limited hyperparameter (HP) transfer across model sizes, and no guarantee that all sub-networks are maximally updated at once. We present \Ours, an elastic transformer that organizes hidden dimensions into a dense core and successive shells, so that every hidden matrix is block lower triangular. One full-width forward pass contains every sub-network's exact hidden states as prefixes, so joint training keeps a fixed computation graph and costs about as much per step as training the widest sub-network alone. We further introduce \muE, an extension of maximal update parameterization (\mup) to \Ours and other elastic architectures. Its scaling rules provably keep all sub-networks of a supernet maximally updated simultaneously (\muI), and keep doing so when the supernet is widened or given more shells; sweeps confirm that HPs tuned on a small non-elastic proxy stay near-optimal for elastic families and larger supernets (\mbox{\muT}). A single \Ours run produces sub-networks that outperform MatFormer and fully elastic baselines at matched parameter counts, and approach separately trained models that together take several times the steps.
original_abstract.source_title: ShellElastic: Scalable Elastic Pretraining with Simultaneous Maximal Updates and Hyperparameter Transfer

en.text: ShellElastic trains nested subnetworks inside one shared Transformer by arranging hidden matrices as a dense core with block-lower-triangular shells. A full-width forward pass preserves each smaller network’s exact hidden-state prefix, enabling a fixed joint-training graph. Its maximal-update extension supports simultaneous subnetwork updates and hyperparameter transfer, with experiments comparing MatFormer, fully elastic and separately trained models. This is relevant to producing recommendation models for multiple serving budgets without wholly separate pretraining runs; recommendation-specific transfer remains untested.

zh.text: ShellElastic把共享Transformer组织成密集核心与分块下三角外层，一次完整宽度前向计算即可保留各小子网的精确隐状态前缀，联合训练的计算图因此固定。其最大更新参数化扩展支持各子网同时学习与超参数迁移，并与MatFormer、全弹性模型和单独训练模型比较。该设计可为一次预训练产出多种服务预算的推荐模型提供参考，推荐场景迁移仍未验证。

original_abstract.text: Linear-attention and state-space LLMs carry long context in a fixed-size recurrent state, and quantizing that state is the natural way to cut its cost during long decode. Unlike a weight tensor, the state is rewritten at every step, so a quantizer applied at each step sits inside the recurrence and its errors compound. INT4 that leaves synthetic recall perfectly intact at the start destroys it a thousand steps later. The mechanism is a feedback between the quantizer scale and the state it is derived from. Yoking that scale to a full-precision reference removes the resulting norm explosion entirely, yet recovers only 1.8 of the 5.4 nats lost, so numerical instability and functional degradation are separable failures. The remainder is resolution-dependent, and in our per-step setting every outlier-aware scheme we test loses to plain persistent scaling. Allocating bits across layers does help, but under article-disjoint splits a learned allocation collapses onto the trivial rule of protecting the first few layers. Run out to 32K, group-wise INT4 is worth no more than discarding the state. Contain the scale rather than locate outliers, and report the decode horizon at which a bit-width was certified.
original_abstract.source_title: When Dynamic Scaling Fails: A Scale-State Feedback Governs Recurrent-State Quantization in Linear-Attention and SSM LLMs

en.text: This study separates numerical instability from information loss in quantized recurrent states. Scale–state feedback can cause norm growth, but controlling that scale alone recovers only part of lost performance; finer resolution and long decoding horizons still matter. In the tested settings, group-wise INT4 at 32K decode performs no better than discarding the state, and learned layer precision allocation reduces to protecting early layers under article-disjoint evaluation. The useful warning for compressed recommendation histories is to validate error accumulation over the intended horizon, rather than certify a bit width from short recall tests. In the tested per-step quantization setting, outlier-aware schemes underperform persistent scaling; this comparison is specific to those schemes and that setting.

zh.text: 研究把循环状态量化的数值不稳定与信息损失分开检查：量化尺度和状态之间的反馈可能放大范数，但只控制尺度只能恢复部分损失，量化分辨率和持续解码长度仍重要。在所测设置中，分组INT4持续解码到32K时不优于丢弃状态；按文章隔离评估后，学习得到的逐层精度分配退化为优先保护前几层。对推荐历史压缩的警示是按实际使用长度检查误差积累，不能只凭短序列召回测试认定某比特宽度可靠。 在所测逐步量化设置中，异常值感知方案不及固定尺度方案；这一比较限定于论文测试的方案和设置。

original_abstract.text: Spiking neural networks target energy-efficient language modeling through sparse, binary activations, but the efficiency-accuracy tradeoff of spiking language models is uncharacterized at scale. We present the first Chinchilla-style IsoFLOP scaling study of a spiking language model, sweeping SpikeGPT-family models (RWKV backbone) from width 384 to 1536 across compute budgets from $3\times10^{17}$ to $10^{19}$ FLOPs on FineWeb-EDU. We report two findings. First, the compute-optimal frontier is $N_{opt} \propto C^{0.56}$, close to the 0.50 that Hoffmann et al. report for dense Transformers, so spiking does not change how parameters and data should be traded off under a compute budget. Second, against non-spiking RWKV and Transformer baselines trained the same way, the loss gap splits into a backbone cost of about 0.16 nats that does not change with compute and a spiking cost that falls steadily with compute, from 0.34 to 0.23 nats over our range. These results give the first compute-optimal recipe for spiking language models and quantify the accuracy cost of their sparsity.
original_abstract.source_title: Compute-Optimal Scaling Laws for Spiking Language Models

en.text: This IsoFLOP study evaluates SpikeGPT-family language models across widths 384–1536 and compute budgets of 3×10^17–10^19 FLOPs. The compute-optimal parameter exponent is 0.56. Matched training comparisons separate an approximately 0.16-nat backbone loss cost from a spiking cost that decreases from 0.34 to 0.23 nats with compute. It quantifies accuracy trade-offs in the tested range; it does not measure recommendation performance or hardware energy savings.

zh.text: 该等 FLOPs 研究在宽度 384–1536、计算预算 3×10^17–10^19 FLOPs 范围内评测 SpikeGPT 系列语言模型，得到计算最优参数规模的指数为 0.56。相同训练条件下，损失差距可分为约 0.16 nat 的骨干成本，以及随计算量增加而从 0.34 降至 0.23 nat 的脉冲化成本。它量化了测试范围内的准确率权衡，没有测量推荐表现或硬件节能。

original_abstract.text: Compressing the key-value (KV) cache is essential for serving long-context large language models (LLMs) under memory constraints. While current scalar quantization methods achieve significant compression, they typically face a quality-fidelity trade-off, either suffering from performance instability at 2-bit precision or necessitating 3-bit keys to maintain model quality. In this work, we demonstrate that a uniform low-bit k2v2 configuration (2-bit keys and 2-bit values) can preserve near-baseline quality by using vector quantization (VQ) based on the $E_8$ lattice for KV keys. We show that structured VQ exploits correlations across adjacent dimensions to achieve signal-to-quantization-noise ratios (SQNR) higher than those of independent scalar quantization at the same key payload rate. To ensure practical utility, we adapt a table-based asymmetric scoring algorithm that avoids explicit codebook dequantization during attention computation and preserves decode-throughput parity with scalar baselines. Across five LLM families, our $E_8$ k2v2 approach yields \textasciitilde$6\times$ KV compression, roughly 20\% smaller than scalar k3v2 (3-bit keys and 2-bit values), while retaining near-baseline long-context perplexity. In our full-suite perplexity evaluation, $E_8$ improves over scalar k3v2 in 80\% of model--dataset--context settings. These results indicate that $E_8$ lattice VQ improves quality per byte while keeping throughput at parity, suggesting that structured key quantization is a useful primitive for KV-compression stacks. Overall, our work provides a low-overhead primitive for expanding the quality-memory frontier in long-context LLM inference.
original_abstract.source_title: E8 Lattice Key Quantization for Low-Bit KV-Cache Compression

en.text: E8 lattice vector quantization exploits correlations between key dimensions to support 2-bit keys and values, with table-based attention scoring that avoids explicit codebook decompression. Across five LLM families, it provides roughly 6x KV compression, about 20% less storage than scalar 3-bit-key/2-bit-value quantization, while retaining near-baseline perplexity and throughput parity with scalar baselines. It suggests a memory-efficient primitive whose recommendation applicability is untested.

zh.text: 该研究用E8格点向量量化利用键向量相邻维度的相关性，实现键和值均为2位的KV缓存，并通过查表计算注意力，避免显式解码码本。在五类语言模型中，缓存约压缩六倍，比3位键、2位值的标量方案再小约20%，同时保持接近基线的困惑度和相当的解码吞吐；推荐应用仍待验证。

original_abstract.text: We present DRanker (Disney+ Ranker), a transformer-based multitask ranking model serving personalized recommendations on the Disney+ homepage. We describe the encoder-only architecture over enriched engagement-history sequences paired with a lightweight causal debiasing mechanism, and the inference stack that enables transformer-based ranking at scale. Through iterative development, we systematically evaluated more complex alternatives and found that simpler designs consistently outperformed them on offline metrics, qualitative behavioral evaluation, and in production. Deployed globally, DRanker drives over 1% lift in our key engagement metric and 0.5% lift in daily active users across all experiences powered by the ranker. We share practical lessons on data engineering, debiasing, and architectural choices that shaped our ranking system at scale.
original_abstract.source_title: DRanker: A Transformer-Based Multi-Task Ranking Model for the Disney+ Homepage

en.text: DRanker uses an encoder-only Transformer over enriched engagement histories, a lightweight debiasing mechanism, and a production inference stack to serve multitask Disney+ homepage ranking. The team reports that simpler designs outperform the more complex alternatives they tested, with global deployment yielding over 1% improvement in its key engagement metric and 0.5% in daily active users. The lessons connect history representation, debiasing, and serving efficiency; the production-specific comparison does not establish that simpler models always scale better.

zh.text: DRanker以增强的用户互动历史为输入，结合仅编码器Transformer、轻量去偏机制与生产推理系统，承担Disney+首页多任务排序。团队报告，在其测试范围内较简洁设计优于复杂替代方案；全球部署后关键参与度指标提高超过1%，日活跃用户提高0.5%。其经验连接历史表示、去偏和服务效率，但生产场景内的比较不能证明简单模型总能更好地扩展。

original_abstract.text: Linear attention and recurrent models compress past tokens into a fixed-size state that is updated at every step. However, storing these states in high precision incurs substantial memory and bandwidth costs at large batch sizes, motivating low-bit state quantization. Unlike weights and key--value caches, a recurrent state is requantized after every update, so its quantization errors accumulate across steps. Our analysis shows that these errors are highly coherent across steps, so reducing per-step errors alone is insufficient. This coherence arises mainly from small updates that are lost in rounding. To preserve these updates, we intervene both before and at rounding. Before rounding, we propose Low-Rank Bypass (LRB), which accumulates small updates in a compact low-rank buffer and periodically merges its sufficiently large elements into the state. At rounding, we observe that a state element can even move opposite to its update, and such reversals prove particularly harmful. Therefore, we propose Bounded Directional Rounding (BDR), which rounds reversed elements toward their updates without additional storage. Although BDR enlarges the rounding error, it improves the model, suggesting that the direction of an update matters more than its rounding error at a single step. Across Gated DeltaNet, GLA, Mamba2, and RetNet, our training-free method substantially outperforms INT4, while reducing state memory by up to 5.3$\times$ and speeding up decoding by up to 1.9$\times$ relative to FP32 states.
original_abstract.source_title: Preserving Updates in Low-Bit Recurrent State Quantization

en.text: The paper targets low-bit recurrent-state quantization, where repeated rounding can discard small updates and create correlated errors. A low-rank bypass accumulates these updates, while bounded directional rounding prevents harmful update reversals without extra storage for that rounding rule. Tests on Gated DeltaNet, GLA, Mamba2 and RetNet outperform INT4, with up to 5.3-fold state-memory reduction and 1.9-fold decoding speedup versus FP32 states. Preserving update direction is a useful hypothesis for compressed recommendation histories; the evidence remains on the tested recurrent models.

zh.text: 论文处理低比特循环状态量化：反复舍入会丢失小更新，并产生跨步相关误差。低秩旁路先积累小更新，有界方向舍入则避免更新方向反转，后者本身无需额外存储。在Gated DeltaNet、GLA、Mamba2和RetNet上优于普通INT4；相对FP32状态，状态内存最低约为FP32的1/5.3、解码最多加速1.9倍。保留更新方向可作为推荐历史压缩的实验思路，证据仍限于所测循环模型。

original_abstract.text: Linear attention promises the efficiency needed for long-context language modelling, yet its fixed-size recurrent state must simultaneously support ongoing computation and preserve information from an ever-growing history. This coupling has reinforced a prevailing view that the state's memory capacity defines the model's long-context capability. We challenge this presumed ceiling: \emph{recurrent computation need not bear the full burden of long-term storage}. We introduce NoteBank, a sparse episodic memory that archives selected text before future queries are known, uses the backbone's native features for writing and addressing, and reads retrieved evidence through its native forward computation via replay. This \emph{training-free, plug-and-play} interface requires no external embedding model, separately trained retriever, or separate neural reader. At one million tokens, it raises Gated DeltaNet's mean accuracy across six RULER retrieval tasks from 1.7% to 70.3%, with no observed significant retrieval degradation from 4K to 1M tokens. This recovery adds $\leqslant$0.025% to analytical FLOPs, with persistent context storage approximately 1/2,600 that of a Transformer's full MHA KV cache at matched width, depth, and precision. Experiments extend from three 1.3B recurrent backbones to Mamba-2-8B and post-trained Qwen3.5-9B, demonstrating gains on LongBench v1/v2 and MemoryAgentBench. Together, these results show that sparse evidence storage and native replay can substantially expand the long-context capability of pretrained linear attention models while retaining the efficiency of recurrent computation.
original_abstract.source_title: History Replays Itself: Unleashing Long-Context Capability in Linear Attention

en.text: NoteBank adds a training-free episodic archive to pretrained recurrent models: it stores selected text before future queries are known, retrieves with native model features, and replays evidence through the original backbone. At one million tokens, Gated DeltaNet mean accuracy on six RULER retrieval tasks rises from 1.7% to 70.3%. Its small analytical-FLOPs overhead is not negligible wall-clock overhead, and the storage comparison excludes model weights and transient allocations. Long-history ranking is a possible transfer direction, not a tested CTR result.

zh.text: NoteBank为预训练循环模型加入无需训练的片段档案：在未来查询未知时保存部分文本，利用模型自身特征检索，并把证据重新送入原骨干计算。百万token下，Gated DeltaNet在六项RULER检索任务上的平均准确率由1.7%升至70.3%。较小的理论FLOPs增量不等于实际耗时可忽略，存储比较也不含模型权重和临时分配。长历史排序可借鉴这一结构，但尚无CTR验证。

original_abstract.text: Large-scale personalization is shifting from embedding-table retrieval to LLM-based recommenders that generate the Semantic ID (SID) of the item to recommend, where each SID is a short sequence of discrete hierarchical content codes. A single instruction-tuned model can then unify retrieval, content understanding, and language, and recommend brand-new titles from their content alone using SID; then, how should the model generate the SID? Traditionally, models rely on a single language modeling head that generates tokens autoregressively, typically using constrained beam search. In contrast, an emerging body of work explores multi-token prediction (MTP), where dedicated heads predict all tokens in parallel, substantially reducing the decoding latency associated with beam search. We report an industry-scale, apples-to-apples comparison of these two generation paradigms: single-head autoregressive decoding vs. MTP. We introduce a new auxiliary ranking loss, defined over the joint SID score, to train the MTP objective. We evaluate the SID training objectives on both quality and training/inference cost, inside a multi-task LLM that jointly does personalized retrieval, content question-answering (QA), and instruction following over a large streaming-media catalog. Our experiments show single-head beam search consistently beats MTP on most product-critical metrics: ranking and content QA, and trains at roughly 2.6x lower dollar cost on Qwen3-8B scale; MTP wins only on raw inference throughput. Around this finding, we detail an efficient training and inference stack and report end-to-end gains over the previous non-SID baseline equipped with an auxiliary ranking head: +77% item cold-start ranking, +22% content-QA accuracy, +2.8x faster training, with language metric regression traced to SID vocabulary expansion. We address the language regression by reinforcement learning post training.
original_abstract.source_title: Personalized LLM Recommendation with Semantic IDs: Autoregressive Beam Search vs. Multi-Token Prediction

en.text: In a multitask streaming-media recommender, this study compares autoregressive semantic-ID beam search with parallel multi-token prediction strengthened by an auxiliary ranking loss. With four-code IDs and Qwen3 backbones, beam search performs better on most ranking and content-QA metrics and costs about 1/2.6 as much to train at 8B scale; parallel prediction retains the inference-throughput advantage. The result motivates measuring quality, training cost, and serving throughput together, without assuming the same trade-off for much longer IDs or different task mixtures.

zh.text: 论文在多任务流媒体推荐中，对比语义ID的自回归束搜索与加入辅助排序损失的并行多token预测。在四码字ID和Qwen3骨干的设置下，束搜索在大多数排序与内容问答指标上更好，8B规模训练费用约为后者的1/2.6；并行预测仍有推理吞吐优势。它提示应同时比较质量、训练费用与服务吞吐，不能将结论直接推广到更长ID或不同任务组合。

original_abstract.text:
Semantic-ID-based generative recommendation unifies retrieval and ranking through autoregressive decoding but differs structurally from discriminative models, which can directly access rich target-item side features. The attributes are compressed into a finite codebook during quantization, while the target item remains undetermined during decoding and its features cannot be looked up. This target-side feature vacuum weakens generation at each semantic-ID level through high conditional entropy and cascading errors, and final ranking through missing target-side feature crossing.
  Existing methods interact with candidate representations or generate discrete attribute tokens, but none reconstructs a continuous target-side representation inside decoding to support both stepwise generation and ranking. We propose TacGR (Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation). Before decoding each codeword, TacGR anticipates a continuous target-side feature vector and crosses it with the semantic prefix and user behavior sequence inside the decoder. The crossed representation conditions current-level generation and is directly used for ranking.
  Continuous-vector regression risks a learnable target collapsing with its prediction and prediction noise propagating into generation through attention. TacGR addresses these challenges with a semantic-anchoring auxiliary tower and a unidirectional visibility mask, respectively. For extremely long industrial behavior histories, it introduces gated convolutional denoising to suppress noise and adapts the pyramid memory funnel to reduce inference cost. Offline experiments on a large-scale Lazada dataset show significant gains over OneRec, UniRec, and UniSGR. Online A/B testing improves IPV, Order, and GMV by 0.79%, 5.55%, and 3.09%, respectively.
original_abstract.source_title: UniSGR-V2: Stepwise Target-Side Feature Anticipation and Crossing for Generative Recommendation

en.text: UniSGR-V2 presents TacGR, which predicts a continuous target-side feature vector before each semantic-ID codeword and crosses it with the semantic prefix and user history to support generation and ranking. An anchored auxiliary tower and one-way visibility mask limit collapse and prediction-noise propagation; gated denoising and a pyramid memory funnel handle long histories. In a Lazada homepage A/B test replacing the previous generative recall model, IPV, orders, and GMV rise relatively by 0.79%, 5.55%, and 3.09%; this is not a test replacing the entire CTR ranking stack.

zh.text: UniSGR-V2提出TacGR，在每个语义ID码字生成前预测连续目标侧特征，并与语义前缀、用户历史交叉，用于生成和排序。锚定辅助塔与单向可见性掩码缓解坍塌和预测噪声传播，门控去噪及金字塔记忆漏斗处理长历史。在Lazada首页替换旧生成式召回模型的A/B测试中，商品详情页浏览量、订单量及成交总额分别相对提升0.79%、5.55%和3.09%；实验并未替换完整CTR精排链路。

original_abstract.text: Dynamic sparse training (DST) aims to reduce training costs while maintaining accuracy. Existing DST methods mask out parameters but keep matrix dimensions unchanged. Training speedups therefore depend on specialized support, such as sparse kernels. We introduce BARTER, a structured DST framework that reduces training cost using standard dense kernels by keeping training tensors physically compact while dynamically reallocating capacity across layers. Unlike existing works that require computing gradients for all parameters, BARTER instead uses statistics collected only from active units during ordinary backpropagation to prune and clone attention heads and feed-forward channels under separate fixed global budgets. At each topology update, it resizes the affected parameter tensors and remaps their optimizer states, so subsequent training steps operate directly on the compact model. Training and fine-tuning experiments with Transformer-based vision models on two image classification benchmarks at densities from $0.1$ to $0.7$ show competitive Top-1 accuracy relative to full-tensor DST baselines. On an NVIDIA L40, BARTER achieves speedups of up to $6.29\times$ in measured training segments and reduces peak allocated GPU memory by up to $81.3\%$ relative to these implementations. An iPhone 13 Pro Max training benchmark additionally shows a $2.78\times$ speedup over the full-tensor DST baseline.
original_abstract.source_title: BARTER: Compact Dynamic Sparse Training with Standard Dense Kernels

en.text: BARTER dynamically prunes and clones attention heads and FFN channels while physically resizing tensors and optimizer states, allowing standard dense kernels to train compact models. Vision-transformer experiments at densities 0.1–0.7 report competitive accuracy, up to 6.29× faster measured training segments and 81.3% lower peak allocated GPU memory on L40 versus full-tensor DST implementations. These are segment benchmarks, not complete-run speedups; ranking transfer remains untested.

zh.text: BARTER 动态裁剪与克隆注意力头、FFN 通道，并同步缩小参数张量和映射优化器状态，使标准稠密算子直接训练紧凑模型。在密度 0.1–0.7 的视觉 Transformer 实验中，准确率具有竞争力；相对完整张量 DST 实现，L40 上所测训练片段最高加速 6.29 倍、峰值已分配显存最高下降 81.3%。这是片段测速，并非完整训练任务加速，排序迁移尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Scaling laws predict large-model performance from small experiments, but finding a reliable law itself requires costly experiments. SLDBench tests whether language-model agents can discover scaling laws when all experimental results are given upfront. We introduce SLDBench v2 with two extensions. First, we expand the corpus from 8 to 127 scenarios spanning language-model pretraining, downstream performance, and vision-language transfer, and select 30 challenging scenarios on which a reference power-law fit reaches $R^2 \le 0.8$; they represent at least $1.09 \times 10^{23}$ FLOPs of source-reported training compute. Second, we introduce active scaling law discovery: an agent chooses which experiments to run, pays each one's recorded cost (e.g., training FLOPs), and revises its law as outcomes arrive, and is scored on the same hidden extrapolation targets as in the passive setting. Across 8 frontier agent systems, median $R^2$ drops from 0.72-0.75 (passive) to 0.24-0.57 (active), and prediction error rises 1.5-4.7 times, depending on the system. Agents favor cheap experiments, spending 8-44% of the full-pool cost on average; low-cost acquisition can yield strong predictions, but cheap purchases also leave experimental conditions needed for extrapolation unobserved. Experimental planning thus remains a key open challenge for agents that assist model development in the prevailing AI-for-AI study.
original_abstract.source_title: SLDBench v2: Active Scaling Law Discovery

en.text: SLDBench v2 tests experimental planning for scaling-law discovery through historical replay: agents buy recorded experiments, revise fitted laws, and predict hidden larger-scale outcomes. Across eight agent systems on 30 screened scenarios, active acquisition produces worse extrapolation than receiving all observations upfront; favoring cheap experiments can miss informative scale variation. Costs and prediction quality are reported separately, and prices include estimates/proxies rather than uniformly measured compute. CTR engineering inference: replay existing training sweeps to evaluate acquisition policies before funding new runs, preserving held-out scales and within-domain coverage. This is an empirical methodology benchmark, not a new architecture or CTR result.

zh.text: SLDBench v2 通过历史实验回放评估扩展定律的实验规划：代理付费获取已记录实验的结果，修订拟合规律，再预测隐藏的大规模结果。在筛选出的 30 个场景、八种代理系统中，主动选购数据的外推表现低于预先获得全部观测；偏好便宜实验可能遗漏关键的规模变化。成本与预测质量分开报告，价格含估算和代理指标，并非统一实测计算量。对 CTR 的工程启发是先用历史训练扫描回放评估实验选择策略，再投入新训练，并保留隐藏测试规模和域内覆盖。这是实证方法基准，不是新架构，也没有 CTR 结果。

original_abstract.text: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) improve parameter efficiency by recursively reusing shared Transformer modules, yet their repeated computation over evolving recurrent states poses new challenges for low-bit deployment. Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods, largely designed for feed-forward Transformers, fail to account for cross-loop activation dynamics, heterogeneous loop sensitivity, and recursive error propagation, leading to substantial performance degradation at low precision. To address these challenges, we propose LoopQuant, a loop-aware PTQ framework for accurate and efficient low-bit quantization of LoopLMs. LoopQuant is built on three core components: 1) Cross-Loop Distribution Canonicalization (CLDC) learns a shared quantization-friendly representation across recurrent states while preserving parameter sharing; 2) Interaction-Aware Loop-wise Precision Allocation (ILPA) allocates activation precision under a fixed bit budget by modeling task-level loop sensitivity and cross-loop interactions; and 3) Loop-Conditioned Task Calibration (LCTC) further aligns quantized inference with the low-bit recursive trajectory through lightweight task-space calibration. Extensive experiments across LoopLM architectures demonstrate that LoopQuant consistently outperforms existing low-bit PTQ methods. On Ouro-2.6B, LoopQuant under W4A4 surpasses all W4A8 baselines in performance, while reducing model memory by 65.3% with only 3.4% additional storage overhead over naive INT4 and achieving a 1.7 times decoding speedup over BF16. These results demonstrate a strong balance among accuracy, compression, and inference efficiency, providing a practical and deployment-friendly solution for low-bit LoopLM inference. The code is available at [https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/LoopQuant].
original_abstract.source_title: LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers

en.text: LoopQuant adapts post-training quantization to repeated use of shared Transformer blocks. It canonicalizes cross-loop activation distributions, allocates activation precision by loop sensitivity and interactions, and calibrates the resulting low-bit trajectory. On Ouro-2.6B, the authors report that W4A4 exceeds the tested W4A8 baselines and gives a 1.7-fold decoding speedup versus BF16. This provides a loop-aware compression recipe for parameter-sharing architectures; the reported efficiency and accuracy do not establish gains for CTR models or other hardware configurations.

zh.text: LoopQuant针对共享Transformer模块被反复执行时的量化误差，统一跨循环激活分布，按各轮敏感度与相互作用分配激活精度，再校准低比特循环轨迹。在Ouro-2.6B上，作者报告W4A4优于所测W4A8基线，解码速度为BF16的1.7倍。该方法可供共享参数架构的循环感知压缩参考，但未证明CTR模型或其他硬件配置下具有同样收益。

original_abstract.text: Industrial recommendation rankers keep scaling in width and depth to billions of parameters, but this increasingly incurs costs in parameter growth, distributed communication overhead, and training inefficiency. We introduce \underline{C}hain \underline{D}imension \underline{S}caling (CDS), a scaling strategy orthogonal to width and depth. CDS repeatedly applies a single feature-interaction block with parameters shared across iterations, so the number of iterations (the chain length) becomes a new scaling dimension that adds no parameters. A lightweight intra-chain residual connection stabilizes optimization and improves quality. CDS enables two regimes. In the \emph{compression regime}, shallow blocks with a longer chain match deeper baselines with fewer parameters and faster training; in the \emph{quality-scaling regime}, increasing chain length under a fixed parameter budget yields consistent offline and online gains, suggesting the chain dimension adds modeling capacity beyond parameter reuse. We evaluate CDS in a large-scale multi-task short-video ranking system in production. In the compression regime, CDS stays within $0.03\%$ of baseline offline quality while reducing trainable parameters by 26.6\% and improving training throughput by 6.4\%, with neutral-to-positive online participation. In the quality-scaling regime, quality improves monotonically with chain length. Wall-clock analysis shows the efficiency gain comes mainly not from reduced FLOPs but from lower cross-device synchronization overhead and reduced optimizer update cost. These results position parameter-shared iterative computation as a practical, communication-efficient scaling axis for industrial ranking systems.
original_abstract.source_title: Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking

en.text: CDS scales an industrial recommendation ranker by repeatedly applying a parameter-shared feature-interaction block, with an intra-chain residual connection stabilizing optimization. In a production multitask short-video system, its compression configuration reduces trainable parameters by 26.6% and raises training throughput by 6.4% while retaining near-baseline offline quality. The online engagement estimate has a confidence interval spanning zero. Efficiency gains mainly come from less cross-device synchronization and optimizer-update work, not lower FLOPs; increasing chain length at fixed parameters also improves quality in the tested setting.

zh.text: CDS通过重复执行共享参数的特征交互模块扩展工业排序模型，并用链内残差稳定优化。在生产环境的多任务短视频系统中，压缩配置减少26.6%的可训练参数、提高6.4%的训练吞吐，离线质量接近基线；线上参与度增益的置信区间跨零。效率主要来自跨设备同步和优化器更新开销下降，并非FLOPs减少；实验还显示，固定参数时增加链长可改善质量。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale model capacity efficiently by activating only a small subset of experts for each input, while still requiring all parameters to be stored in memory, resulting in substantial memory overhead. Expert merging techniques have recently emerged as a promising compression paradigm that reduces this overhead by consolidating multiple experts into a smaller set. However, existing approaches have two key limitations: (i) direct convex interpolation in parameter space is not generally guaranteed to yield meaningful interpolation of expert functions; and (ii) estimating expert similarity or merging coefficients often relies on calibration data, introducing dependence on the calibration distribution. To address these limitations, we propose Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging (SLEM), a calibration-free expert merging framework that occurs in a structured latent representation of expert weights using a VAE. SLEM groups experts within and across layers based on latent similarities and derives merging coefficients from expert weight spectra. It then performs geometry-aware latent interpolation and decodes the resulting representations into merged expert weights. Compared with existing expert merging methods, SLEM achieves comparable or better performance on general knowledge benchmarks and higher average performance on generation benchmarks involving mathematical reasoning and code generation.
original_abstract.source_title: SLEM: Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging

en.text: SLEM compresses MoE expert storage by training a variational autoencoder on expert weights, pairing experts through latent similarity, and merging them within or across layers using spectrum-derived coefficients and latent interpolation. It needs no input calibration dataset, but does require VAE training and model-dependent rank choices. Tests on three language models show competitive knowledge-task results and stronger average math/code generation than compared merging methods; higher compression still loses quality versus uncompressed models. CTR engineering inference: evaluate weight-only expert consolidation when calibration traffic is unavailable, including compression preparation cost and slice-level regression checks. No CTR experiments are reported.

zh.text: SLEM 在专家权重上训练变分自编码器，按潜在表示相似度将专家配对，再结合权重谱确定的系数与潜在空间插值，在层内或跨层合并专家以减少存储。它不需要输入校准数据，但仍需训练 VAE，并选择与模型相关的谱秩。在三种语言模型中，知识任务表现具有竞争力，数学与代码生成的平均表现优于所比较合并方法；较高压缩率下仍不及未压缩模型。对 CTR 的工程启发是在缺少校准流量时评估仅依赖权重的专家合并，同时计入压缩准备成本并检查分域退步。本文没有 CTR 实验。

original_abstract.text: Relevance prediction between user queries and items is a fundamental component of e-commerce search systems. Traditionally, high-quality relevance labels are obtained through human judgment, which is reliable but expensive, slow, and difficult to scale. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) enable automated relevance judgment at scale, achieving performance comparable to human annotators. However, such systems often rely on large commercial LLMs with complex prompts, resulting in high inference costs and limited throughput. In this work, we propose a framework that bridges this gap by distilling a high-performing LLM-based relevance judgment system into efficient multimodal student models. We first curate a small, high-quality human-annotated dataset to serve as ground truth. Using this dataset, we develop a reliable LLM-as-a-judge pipeline through careful prompt engineering and iterative refinement. This pipeline is then used to generate large-scale relevance labels, which serve as training data for compact multimodal models. Our distilled models achieve performance close to the teacher system while significantly improving latency, cost, and scalability. This approach enables practical deployment of high-quality relevance prediction systems in production environments.
original_abstract.source_title: From a Large-Scale Teacher to Efficient Multimodal Students for Search Relevance Prediction

en.text: This search-relevance framework uses a small human-labeled set to refine an LLM judge, then distills its large-scale labels into compact multimodal student models. The students approach teacher quality while improving serving cost and throughput, offering a route to scale query–item relevance supervision. Evaluation distinguishes a test set used during teacher-prompt refinement from a separate cleaner test set; this is relevance-label distillation, not evidence of an online CTR gain.

zh.text: 该搜索相关性框架先用小规模人工标注集改进大模型评判流程，再用教师生成的大量标签训练紧凑的多模态学生模型。学生在接近教师质量的同时改善服务成本和吞吐，为扩展查询—商品相关性监督提供路径。评测区分了参与教师提示调优的测试集与较独立的测试集；这属于相关性标签蒸馏，并非线上CTR提升证据。

original_abstract.text: We introduce FORGE (Fast On-chip Rotor Generation for Experts), a procedural weight generation system for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference. Rather than storing and loading every expert weight tensor from HBM, we show how a compact accelerator inside each Streaming Multiprocessor can regenerate them on-the-fly from $O(\log^2 d)$ rotor parameters per projection. Per replaced layer, gigabytes of stored expert weights are approximated with under a megabyte of seeds. This addresses the dual memory bottleneck of autoregressive Sparse MoE decode, where per-expert FFN operations are HBM-bandwidth-bound at small routed-token counts and the aggregate expert footprint forces multi-node Expert Parallelism (EP) with all-to-all traffic. We realize the approach as the Rotor Generation Unit (RGU), a fixed-function datapath that generates FFN weight tiles without competing with Tensor Core execution. With 30% of the MoE FFN layers replaced across five Sparse MoE models, we estimate 1.3-2.8x higher system throughput at matched GPU count and 1.10-1.15x lower per-user decode latency at short context. In exchange, downstream accuracy on three model families falls below that of the same model fine-tuned without rotor replacement, and the replacement ratio controls this tradeoff. FORGE also expands KV cache capacity by 1.2-2.6x. It is agnostic to the bit width at which weights are stored, so it can compose with quantization. The RGU is fully implemented/verified in SystemVerilog at ~0.9% SM area overhead (0.032 mm^2/SM, 7nm).
original_abstract.source_title: FORGE: Procedural Weight Generation for Sparse MoE Inference

en.text: FORGE proposes a hardware unit that regenerates approximate MoE expert weights from compact rotor parameters instead of loading full tensors. With 30% of FFN layers replaced, the authors estimate 1.3–2.8x system throughput at matched GPU count and 1.10–1.15x lower short-context per-user decode latency, with downstream accuracy losses. The verified SystemVerilog design is a hardware proposal; these system estimates are not measured recommender deployment gains.

zh.text: MoE推理需要保存并搬运大量专家权重。FORGE设计专用硬件单元，从紧凑参数即时生成近似权重；替换30%的前馈层时，作者估计同GPU数量下系统吞吐提升1.3—2.8倍，短上下文单用户解码延迟改善1.10—1.15倍，但下游准确率下降。其SystemVerilog设计经过验证，系统收益仍是估计，不能视为推荐部署实测。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval (GR) offers a promising paradigm for industrial search by unifying candidate generation within an autoregressive framework. However, effectively leveraging user behaviors in industrial GR remains challenging: existing SID tokenization methods struggle to preserve collaborative signals while maintaining balanced codebook utilization, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) for prioritizing high-value candidates suffers from sparse rewards when generated SIDs fail to match positive items. To address these challenges, we propose WeGR, a unified GR framework with two complementary components. Specifically, the Collaborative and Collapse-free Tokenizer (CoCo-VAE) injects query-to-item and item-to-item collaborative signals into continuous representations before quantization, preserving behavioral information without disrupting codebook optimization. It further couples first-layer codebook refresh to reactivate underutilized codewords with fidelity anti-collapse regularization, which broadens gradient coverage over relevant codewords and penalizes collisions in deeper layers to yield behavior-aware SIDs with balanced utilization. For preference alignment, Dynamic Horizon Policy Optimization (DHPO) progressively expands reward evaluation and policy optimization horizons to alleviate reward sparsity, enabling coarse-to-fine preference learning from SID prefixes to complete items without auxiliary reward models. Extensive offline experiments validate that WeGR improves retrieval and ranking performance. Moreover, a six-week online A/B test on a large-scale e-commerce search platform achieves relative gains of 2.539% in orders, 1.508% in CTR, and 1.381% in CVR, while reducing CPU and GPU usage by 25.5% and 26.1%. These results highlight the effectiveness and efficiency of WeGR in industrial deployment, supporting multiple search scenarios and tens of millions of daily page views.
original_abstract.source_title: WeGR: Towards Unified Generative Retrieval via Behavior-aware Tokenization and Preference Alignment

en.text: WeGR addresses weak collaborative signals and sparse exact-ID rewards in generative retrieval. CoCo-VAE injects behavioral information before quantization and combats codebook collapse; DHPO progressively expands reward and optimization horizons. A six-week industrial e-commerce A/B test reports relative gains of 2.539% in orders, 1.508% in CTR and 1.381% in CVR, alongside 25.5% CPU and 26.1% GPU savings. These are system-level deployment results, not isolated generator-kernel speedups.

zh.text: WeGR 针对生成式检索中的协同信号不足和精确 ID 匹配奖励稀疏，用 CoCo-VAE 在量化前注入行为信息并缓解码本坍塌，用 DHPO 逐步扩大奖励与优化范围。六周工业电商 A/B 测试报告订单、CTR、CVR 分别相对提升 2.539%、1.508%、1.381%，同时节省 25.5% CPU 和 26.1% GPU 用量。这些是系统级部署结果，不能视为生成器内核单独提速。

original_abstract.text: Linear-time sequence models typically store long-context information in a recurrent state. A fixed-size state limits how much information can be stored, while hybrid architectures that add full attention for better recall incur quadratic sequence cost. Alternatively, sparse attention with continued pretraining (CPT) can extend the effective context length. Generalization beyond the trained length remains challenging, however, and CPT can be costly. We introduce FreeSolo, a native sparse attention mechanism with a short-range sliding window branch and a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention. Its linear-time variant, FS-L, learns to prune the prefix before query-dependent selection through short CPT. FS-B searches balanced trees with $O(N\log^2 N)$ algorithmic cost including radix-sort construction. FreeSolo demonstrates better zero-shot length extrapolation than the baselines without long-context fine-tuning.
original_abstract.source_title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation

en.text: FreeSolo avoids forcing all long-context information into a fixed recurrent state by combining a sliding-window branch with a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention. FS-L learns prefix pruning through short continued pretraining and has linear-time sequence cost; FS-B searches balanced trees with O(N log^2 N) cost including radix-sort construction. The paper reports stronger zero-shot length extrapolation than its baselines without long-context fine-tuning. The variants have different memory and complexity trade-offs, and the abstract does not establish gains on recommendation workloads.

zh.text: FreeSolo 将滑动窗口注意力与选择关键单元、直接访问原始 token 的长距离分支结合，避免把全部长上下文信息压入固定大小的循环状态。FS-L 通过短期继续预训练学习前缀剪枝，序列计算成本为线性；FS-B 搜索平衡树，计入基数排序建树后复杂度为 O(N log^2 N)。论文报告其在不进行长上下文微调的情况下，零样本长度外推优于所比较的基线。两种变体的内存与计算取舍不同，摘要未证实推荐负载上的收益。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation models have shown promising results by representing items as semantic IDs and generating these IDs autoregressively. We introduce an approach showing that explicitly incorporating hierarchical and attribute-level supervision into generative recommendation can simultaneously improve training efficiency and long-tail recommendation performance. Existing approaches typically optimize semantic ID prediction with a standard causal cross-entropy objective, which does not explicitly exploit the hierarchical structure of semantic IDs and can require substantial training to learn effective item representations. Moreover, data-sparse tail items often suffer from poor representations due to limited supervision, resulting in weaker long-tail recommendation performance. We address these challenges with HASTE (Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for generaTive rEcommendation), a unified training framework that introduces hierarchical and attribute-specific supervision. HASTE's Hierarchical Loss explicitly exploits the multi-level structure of semantic IDs, providing supervision at each level of the item hierarchy and substantially accelerating training convergence. Its Attribute-Specific Losses encourage the model to preserve fine-grained item attributes, leveraging the language model's inherent semantic knowledge to improve representations and recommendations for tail items. We extensively evaluate HASTE on a fashion recommendation benchmark and across multiple domains of the Amazon dataset. HASTE improves recommendation performance across datasets and item-frequency regimes. Notably, the Hierarchical Loss achieves approximately 2x faster convergence than the standard causal cross-entropy objective, substantially improving training efficiency while maintaining strong recommendation quality.
original_abstract.source_title: HASTE: Hierarchical and Attribute-aware Supervision for Generative Recommendation

en.text: HASTE adds hierarchical and item-attribute supervision to semantic-ID generative recommendation, aiming to reduce training effort and improve representations of infrequent items. Hierarchical loss supervises each ID level, while attribute losses preserve fine-grained semantics. Fashion and Amazon experiments report gains across item-frequency groups; the approximately 2x convergence improvement measures training steps to a validation-loss threshold, not a demonstrated 2x end-to-end wall-clock speedup.

zh.text: HASTE为语义ID生成式推荐加入分层监督与商品属性监督，以减少训练开销并改善低频商品的表示。分层损失监督各级ID，属性损失保留细粒度语义。时尚推荐及Amazon实验报告不同频次商品均有收益；约2倍收敛改善指达到验证损失阈值所需的训练步数，不等于已证明端到端耗时减半。
